_comment: SmartCuff GUI update manifest. Fetched by the installed GUI over plain
public HTTPS -- there is deliberately NO credential in the client. See
README.md for why an embedded token was rejected.
This file is the ONLY thing the updater needs to read. Keep it small and
keep it valid JSON: a malformed manifest must fail soft in the client, but
there is no reason to rely on that.
The installer is a GitHub Release asset rather than a repository blob.
Keep installer_url version-specific: an existing manifest must always
resolve to the exact immutable bytes whose size and SHA-256 it declares.
notes:
Pressure and oscillations are now recorded and reported in mmHg; signed flow is in L/min. Original volts and native acquisition times are retained. Missing calibration is marked unavailable.

Simulator sweeps can run multiple selected protocols for each settings combination. Each protocol runs one cycle per trial with a 30-second vented break. Preview, settings CSV imports/exports, filenames and results identify each trial's protocol.

Each trial gains a simple measurements CSV and a four-panel overview at the front of its PDF: pressure, pulse/envelope, flow, and pump/valve duty. Simulator sweeps also write a short results.csv, and pulse-volume filenames explicitly use mL. Live status, Fit All, and measurement labels use their correct physical units.

This GUI update retains firmware rev27v-followup-288, existing controls, and device calibrations. Unit conversion does not establish absolute flow accuracy or independent MAP accuracy; remaining bench investigations are documented in the simulator collection.
_channel_note: stable is the only channel today. If a test channel is ever added, publish
a second manifest (version-beta.json) rather than adding branching logic to
the client -- the client stays a dumb fetch-and-compare.
